content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"Ballistic Missile Defense Sensors (program element 0603884C) is a Missile Defense Agency (MDA) program that funds a network of layered sensors—land- and sea-based radars—that provide situational awareness and fire-control data for the command and control of missile-defense weapon systems such as Ground-Based Midcourse Defense (GMD), Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD), and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD).","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"The suite of remote ground-based sensors provides early warning, midcourse, and terminal missile-defense threat data, enabling layered detection and tracking of missile targets and delivering fire-control quality position, velocity, and discrimination data through GMD Fire Control or the Command and Control, Battle Management and Communications (C2BMC) system.","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"The program develops, delivers, and deploys the Army Navy/Transportable Radar Surveillance and Control-2 (AN/TPY-2) radars, which can operate as either a THAAD Fire Unit Radar (terminal mode) or a Forward-Based Radar, and are transportable to respond to geographical changes in threats.","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"The sensor network includes the U.S. Space Force COBRA DANE radar at Eareckson Air Station, Alaska, and Upgraded Early Warning Radars at Beale Air Force Base, California; Cape Cod Space Force Station, Massachusetts; Clear Space Force Station, Alaska; Royal Air Force Fylingdales in the United Kingdom; and Pituffik Space Base in Greenland, for defense of the homeland.","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"The program is organized into several projects, including BMDS Radars (project MD11), Cyber Operations (project MC11), and Program-Wide Support (project MD40).","citation":{"fact_id":"70449a7b4ca5973a"}},{"text":"The BMDS Radars project develops future AN/TPY-2, COBRA DANE, Long Range Discrimination Radar (LRDR), Sea Based X-Band (SBX), and Upgraded Early Warning Radar capabilities through system engineering, software development, and testing support, and develops advanced discrimination algorithms to help identify lethal and non-lethal objects.","citation":{"fact_id":"70449a7b4ca5973a"}},{"text":"The Cyber Operations project funds cybersecurity engineering, plans and tests cybersecurity controls, and maintains Risk Management Framework authorizations for the Ground Sensors managed information systems.","citation":{"fact_id":"83cf548efd9db95e"}},{"text":"Program-Wide Support covers non-headquarters management costs supporting MDA functions across the entire Missile Defense System, including government civilians and contract support services, and is allocated on a pro-rata basis across most Agency program elements.","citation":{"fact_id":"279ab047ab33fc53"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"Overlapping coverage from geographically diverse sensors improves threat track data, reduces the impact of the loss of any one sensor, and reduces the potential impact of countermeasures, while extended coverage and accuracy increase the defensive footprint and conserve interceptor inventory.","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"The budget submission reflects a change in national defense policy: the President's January 27, 2025 Executive Order set a goal of protecting U.S. citizens, safeguarding critical infrastructure, and securing second-strike capability against missile attack from any adversary, and the MDA describes responding with speed and intensity to deliver next-generation defenses against ballistic, hypersonic, cruise, and other advanced missile threats.","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"The program's total funding rose from $209.0 million in fiscal year 2025 to $672.6 million in fiscal year 2026, an increase of about $463.6 million.","citation":{"fact_id":"5dc88a3cd652142a"}},{"text":"That change represents a roughly 222% year-over-year increase from fiscal year 2025 to fiscal year 2026—a large swing flagged in GovBudget's feed.","citation":{"fact_id":"5dc88a3cd652142a"}},{"text":"Much of the fiscal year 2026 increase comes from a $475.0 million reconciliation request, which is separate from the $197.6 million discretionary request for the same year.","citation":{"fact_id":"7744c3b4f775c007"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is managed by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) and funded through the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"f50dfeb49fcc11a3"}},{"text":"Lobbying filings by Lockheed Martin Corporation referenced defense appropriations and authorization measures matching the terms 'Missile' and 'Sensors,' including a 2026 filing on the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026 that mentioned space and missile defense issues.","citation":{"fact_id":"002d7f7f516bc2f9"}},{"text":"Lockheed Martin filings in 2025 also referenced the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, Title II, matching the terms 'Missile' and 'Sensors.'","citation":{"fact_id":"1de4f074700ded6d"}},{"text":"The Boeing Company reported lobbying on the FY24 Department of Defense Appropriations Act in a 2024 filing that matched the term 'Missile.'","citation":{"fact_id":"005fc74423472220"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
